cards.description:
## User-reported core issue —3November2026
Jason: the same sort of playback in Open Play is much quieter than Serato/other apps. Exact compared track/settings/device/OS volume were not captured. Treat as a core gain-staging/calibration issue, not proven proprietary-DSP mismatch.

Native138 current session: Master Output−10dB, trackgainA−7/B−3.2dB, channel faders80%, trim0, AutoGainON/reference92, hiddenMixerMasterVolume100%, Linearcrosscentre/amount50/upfader50, filtersOff. Source output stage reserves3dB. Derived from rounded controls: roughly−21.94dBA/−18.14dBB vs original file below limiting; this is NOT measured Serato difference. Fresh app master defaults0dB;−10 is restored session state. Source tracing shows the separate gains; no demonstrated double application. Current-engine raw-forward PCM is now captured: with controlled track gain−7dB, fader80%, neutral EQ/trim, linear centre crossfader and Master Volume100%, measured source-to-output loss is−21.9382dB at master−10 and−11.9382dB at master0. The10dB difference is exact within Float32 precision. Independent decoding/hash/RMS checks cover all8complete stereo witness buffers,44100alignedframes/channel/case. No extra attenuation or limiter reduction in this measured path; this is not a Serato comparison.

## Acceptance
- [x] Record current gain chain/settings and preserve stopped session; no loudness change while owner is away.
- [x] Focused physically-muted current-engine PCM capture with the observed A gain staging versus neutral master; expected ratios, finite output, limiter inactive.117controls/6previews retained; cleanup stopped/muted. No broad matrix.
- [ ] Same local track/section, same output device and OS volume, equivalent Serato mode/master/AutoGain/channel/crossfader settings. Serato performance0dB and offline100% are different controls.
- [ ] If measured unintended attenuation exists, fix its shared owner once; preserve headroom, limiter and gain persistence. Do not blindly boost all songs or change manual saved levels.
- [ ] Owner safe-level listening comparison when available; retain any clipping/headroom/perceived-loudness limitations. Reported issue stays OPEN until supported.

Source-only62line diagnostic added using existing silent capture worklet. No product DSP/default/saved-gain change or new desktop build. First observation export truncated large PCM strings; retained failure, changed export to chunks, repeated only the same two captures once and independently verified complete buffers. Raw musical PCM stays ignored locally. Settings tab restored; main138 paused161.797/111.183s/25tracks/silent. Controls/layouts/library previews, original media and recordings retained.

## Checkpoint188 — actual native two-local-track path, 19 October
0.1.23 normal macOS chooser imported two different real MP3s and loaded one per deck; both independently and simultaneously played/paused. Fader-zero and crossfader isolation/restoration observed in actual master meter. Normal REC/Save produced private745418B Opus; decoded78.96s/stereo48k, finite/positive and peak<1. Files reports2saved/0session-only. Not musical/manual/Sync/headphone/controller acceptance. Disconnected Hercules route blocked Play until Devices Refresh→Use selected output recovered default stereo. Both music BPMs remain unknown (periodic candidates but low confidence); this core blocker is next. ANA-001 visual-waveform fix now open from Jason's report. Both decks stopped, no completion applied. Review: docs/prototype/CORE_DJ_188_OBSERVATION.json. Keep goal core-only.

## Sole active goal — Jason's 19 October instruction
Only CORE-001 is active. Before each action, it must directly enable or verify this two-track DJ workflow. If work drifts to extras, stop that activity immediately and return to the next core blocker. Quick wins and full parity are parked until this milestone is achieved or Jason changes scope.

## Outcome — core DJ experience first
Jason's 19 October correction governs sequencing: take two different music files from his hard drive (MP3 first), put one on each deck, play, cue, mix and beatmatch. Equivalent basic workflow to two turntables and a mixer. Preserve the interface and existing implementation; fix concrete blockers. Full Serato parity remains the long-term backlog.

## Acceptance — one practical end-to-end session
- Import two different real local MP3s through the normal file chooser; original files remain untouched. Load A on deck 1 and B on deck 2, with readable titles/waveforms and independent transport.
- Play/pause and seek both decks independently; temporary cue/hold/release and track replacement behave predictably.
- Listen to one deck on master while privately cueing the other at channel fader zero. Check cue selection, headphone level and cue/master mix, then both cue combinations. Speakers/master and headphone routing are separate.
- Mix with both channel gains/faders, crossfader, master level and meters. Confirm channel/crossfader endpoints and no unexpected clipping at the declared test levels.
- With Sync off, change pitch in the correct direction, nudge/jog to align beats, and complete an audible manual transition. Pitch range/reset must not unexpectedly jump.
- Engage/disengage Sync with two musical tracks and usable BPM/grids; establish and sustain a transition, then return to manual control. A Sync label or matching BPM number alone does not pass.
- Hear low/mid/high EQ and filter/cutoff changes on each channel; return controls to neutral. Main channel filtering is core; the 55-effect catalog is later.
- Exercise the Hercules core controls in this same workflow: browse/load both decks, Play/Cue, pitch, jog/nudge, channel/crossfaders, gain/EQ/filter and headphone controls that the device actually exposes. Record unsupported/unverified controls explicitly.
- Stop both decks and confirm silence/no queued restart. Capture exact app version/source and concise observed results; retain any real blocker.

## Order / dependencies / owner
Owner: Codex implementation; Jason supplies final audible/manual/controller confirmation when present. First normal import→load→play, then mixer/PFL, manual beatmatch, Sync and core controller coverage. Reuse the versioned 0.1.23 desktop baseline and prior per-control evidence, but do not equate old demos/generated tones or current browser code with this session. Preserve its profile, 272 Alternative mappings and previous builds; no wholesale rewrite. Local desktop testing is already approved. Exact candidate and physical availability must be refreshed before playback.

## Pragmatic testing
One practical session with focused checks at changed audio/routing/transport boundaries. Rerun a check only for a change, failure or unresolved risk. Prepare software without timed MIDI captures while Jason is away. Controller may remain unplugged until the physical stage. Software-only evidence cannot establish speakers/headphones/manual mixing. Do not mark this card complete until the practical criteria above are observed.

## Later / review trigger
Stems, sampler compositions, advanced FX, video, four-deck breadth, CDJ/HID/DVS and comprehensive vendor/device parity remain tracked; they do not delay this milestone. Actual timecode/vinyl integration is a separate later task. After Jason completes a two-track mix, review quick-win candidates: library search, simple crates, saved-session recovery. Only pick a small confirmed gap with no new architectural dependency. Any core blocker interrupts extras immediately.

## Execution models — recommendations, not executions
Codex: gpt-6.1-sol, reasoning high, for routine import/UI/mapping work and focused fixes. Escalate only a reproduced unresolved DSP/clock/routing failure to gpt-6-astra/high with the failing artifact. Claude Code review alternative: claude-sonnet-5/high; unresolved DSP review claude-opus-5/high. Keep each linked feature's existing model/effort recommendation. Confirm installed equivalents before invocation; no automatic agent/Claude launch.
